definitions.explanation: A special envelope used to present monetary condolence gifts at Japanese funerals and memorial services.

examples.japanese: {香典袋|こうでんぶくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
{香典袋|こうでんぶくろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: Write your name on the condolence envelope.

examples.japanese: ⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{香典袋|こうでんぶくろ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{売|う}っている→売る：00906_uru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{急|きゅう}→急：13042_kyuu⟧な⟦{葬儀|そうぎ}→葬儀：15337_sougi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{安心|あんしん}→安心：01288_anshin⟧だ。
examples.english: Condolence envelopes are sold at convenience stores, so you can manage even a sudden funeral.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{香典|こうでん}→香典：06127_kouden⟧ (condolence money) and ⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧ (bag/envelope), with ⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧ voiced to ぶくろ through rendaku. These envelopes are sold at stationery stores, convenience stores, and supermarkets. They come in varying levels of formality, with more elaborate designs (featuring black and white or silver mizuhiki cords) used for larger sums.

ETIQUETTE:
The giver's full name is written in black ink on the front, and the amount enclosed is written on the inner envelope. Bills should be older (not crisp new bills), as new bills could imply the death was anticipated.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {香典袋|こうでんぶくろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: to put money in a condolence envelope
- {香典袋|こうでんぶくろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{書|か}き{方|かた}→書き方：13054_kakikata⟧: how to write on a condolence envelope
